applies a rate - cap - based fallback when episode - based routing would otherwise increase upstream concurrency beyond safe thresholds. design summary : the new episodeorchestrator component lives in perf - canary / orchestrator and integrates with the existing probe scheduler. episodes are detected by a lightweight state machine ( idle - > collecting - > quiesce ) using a tunable inter - arrival threshold and minimum episode size. statistical aggregation supports weighted quantile merging so short episodes do not dominate long ones. the rate - cap fallback is a conservative gate : when projected cutover qps would exceed configured rate caps for the target pool, traffic is throttled and progressively ramped using a token - bucket - like controller with backoff.

item.aggregated_output: # Agent Guidelines for Langfuse Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform for developing, monitoring, evaluating, and debugging AI applications. ## How To Work - Read the minimal local context required for the task. - Keep changes scoped and avoid unrelated refactors. - If you are about to write a `useEffect` — or sync fetched data into state, or wire form initial values from loaded data — read `.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md` first. Most such effects should not exist. - For bug fixes, write the failing test first, confirm it fails, then fix the bug. If the bug depends on a data shape, pause and ask: can `pnpm run seed` prefill that shape locally? If not, consider extending a seeder scenario so the bug stays cheaply reproducible (`packages/shared/scripts/seeder/AGENTS.md`), or note why a seed cannot express it. - For user-visible frontend changes in `web/**`, review the affected flow in a real browser before signoff. Prefill the data the flow needs with the seed CLI (`pnpm run seed -- list` shows scenarios; runs print UI deep links) — never with ad-hoc scripts or raw ClickHouse inserts. - When fixing an isolated styling issue in an individual component, read `.agents/skills/storybook/SKILL.md` create or update a component story following its guidance first. - Every PR auto-builds (via GitHub Actions) a disposable, full-stack preview at `pr-.preview.langfuse.com` — nothing to spin up. Use the `langfuse-previews` skill to use or debug one, e.g. read a preview's web/worker error logs with `kubectl`. - For documentation screenshots in Markdown, avoid fixed `height` on `` tags; prefer Markdown images or width-only HTML so previews preserve aspect ratio. - When working on the search bar or any filtering UI/grammar, read `web/src/features/search-bar/README.md` first. It owns the grammar ↔ `FilterState` contract, the validate/lower parity invariants, and the cross-view extension playbook — the bar is intended to become the primary filter interface for every filterable view, so new filtering work extends it through that contract rather than forking it. - When adding or modifying any chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Do not add or widen ESLint disable comments or config overrides without explicit user approval for the exact rule and scope. - Always quote file paths in shell commands, or use `noglob` for path-heavy commands, to avoid zsh glob expansion issues with dynamic Next.js routes. - Never invoke Node-installed binaries through `./node_modules/.bin/*`. Always run them through `pnpm`. - Never commit secrets or credentials. Keep `.env*.example` files in sync with required env vars. ## Project Structure ```text langfuse/ |- web/ # Next.js app (UI + tRPC + public REST) |- worker/ # Queue consumers and background processing |- packages/shared/ # Shared domain, DB, queue contracts, repositories |- ee/ # Enterprise package consumed by web |- generated/ # Generated API clients (do not hand-edit) |- fern/ # API definition sources `- scripts/ # Repo scripts ``` - Dependency direction: - `web` -> `@langfuse/shared`, `@langfuse/ee` - `worker` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/ee` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/shared` -> no imports from `web`, `worker`, or `ee` - Queue payload schemas and queue-name contracts are owned by `packages/shared/src/server/queues.ts`. - High-signal shared entry points: - Domain models: `packages/shared/src/domain/{observations,traces,scores}.ts` - Postgres schema: `packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma` - ClickHouse migrations: `packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/{clustered,unclustered}/*.sql` - Architecture principles live in `.agents/ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md`. ## Core Commands - Install deps: `pnpm install` - Dev all packages: `pnpm run dev` - Dev web only: `pnpm run dev:web` - Dev worker only: `pnpm run dev:worker` - Lint all: `pnpm run lint` - Typecheck all: `pnpm run typecheck` / `pnpm tc` - Run a single test file (vitest filters on the filename argument): - web server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` (client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client `) - worker: `pnpm --filter worker run test ` - shared: `pnpm --filter @langfuse/shared run test ` - Build check: `pnpm run build:check` - Full build: `pnpm run build` - Worktree bootstrap: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` - Worktree maintenance: `bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` - Install Playwright Chromium: `pnpm run playwright:install` ## Local Data Inspection - For feature testing and debugging, inspect the local databases directly when it helps you understand the existing test data. Prefer read-only queries, and continue to use the seed CLI to create frontend test state rather than ad-hoc inserts. - Dev Docker Compose exposes these clients on `${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}`: - Postgres: `PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres}" psql -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}" -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres}"` - ClickHouse: `clickhouse client --host "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" --port "${CLICKHOUSE_NATIVE_PORT:-9000}" --user "${CLICKHOUSE_USER:-clickhouse}" --password "${CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD:-clickhouse}" --database default` - Redis: `REDISCLI_AUTH="${REDIS_AUTH:-myredissecret}" redis-cli -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${REDIS_HOST_PORT:-6379}"` - If any connection fails, check `docker-compose.dev.yml` for local override variables and confirm the services are running. ## Verification - `web/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted web tests. - `worker/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted worker tests. - `packages/shared/**` non-schema changes: `pnpm run lint` plus one targeted web check and one targeted worker check. - `packages/shared/prisma/**` or `packages/shared/clickhouse/**`: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run db:generate`, and targeted web/worker regressions. - Public API contracts in `web/src/pages/api/public/**`, `web/src/features/public-api/types/**`, or `fern/apis/**`: `pnpm run lint`, targeted server API tests, and Fern update/regeneration. - Cross-package refactors: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and targeted tests for impacted packages. - Client-bundle soundness: CI scans every prod web build (`pnpm run scan:client-bundle`) for minifier-dropped bindings and Node-only globals leaking into browser chunks — the SWC dropped-binding class ships runtime-only `ReferenceError`s that dev builds and type checks cannot see (LFE-10645). On failure, `scripts/scan-client-bundle.mjs`'s header explains the canonical fix. End your turn with evidence, not claims: quote each check's summary line — e.g. `Tasks: 8 successful, 8 total` (turbo lint/typecheck) or `Tests 12 passed (12)` (vitest) — say which checks you skipped and why, never report unverified work as done, and never end with work pending. ## Generated Files Do not hand-edit generated or build artifacts: - `generated/*` - `web/.next/*` - `web/.next-check/*` - `*/dist/*` - `packages/shared/prisma/generated/*` Public API contract changes must update Fern sources in `fern/apis/**` and regenerated outputs. Never hand-edit `generated/**`. ## Shared Agent Setup - `.agents/AGENTS.md` is the canonical root guide. - Root `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`. - Root `CLAUDE.md` is a compatibility symlink to `AGENTS.md`. - When creating or editing `.agents/skills/**`, use `.agents/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`; keep skills concise with progressive disclosure. - After changing shared agent setup, run `pnpm run agents:sync` and `pnpm run agents:check`. - Generated provider config and shim outputs under `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.codex/`, `.vscode/`, or `.mcp.json` are local artifacts, not source of truth files. # Codex Guidelines for `web` This file covers package-local guidance for this package. Use root [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for monorepo-level rules. ## Purpose - Next.js application with UI, tRPC backend, and public REST API routes. - Check `web/package.json` for current Next.js, React, and tRPC versions before version-sensitive work. - Primary package for frontend and most request/response surface changes. ## Maintenance Contract - `AGENTS.md` is a living document. - Update this file in the same PR when material web-local changes occur: - new/renamed web entry points - new API route families - changed web-specific verification commands - If the change also affects monorepo workflows or other packages, update root `AGENTS.md` too. ## High-Signal Entry Points - App shell/providers: `src/pages/_app.tsx` - tRPC context/procedures: `src/server/api/trpc.ts` - tRPC router registry: `src/server/api/root.ts` - tRPC routers: `src/server/api/routers/*`, `src/features/*/server/*` - Public REST API routes: `src/pages/api/public/*` - Unstable public eval APIs: `src/pages/api/public/unstable/{evaluators,evaluation-rules}/*` - Feature modules: `src/features/*` - Reusable UI components: `src/components/*` - Tests: - Server integration tests: `src/__tests__/server/*.servertest.ts` - Server unit tests: `src/__tests__/server/unit/*.servertest.ts` - Client tests: `src/**/*.clienttest.ts(x)` - E2E: `src/__e2e__/*` ## Shared Package Imports - Prefer `@langfuse/shared` in frontend-safe web code for shared types, zod schemas, domain contracts, table definitions, prompt/eval/model-pricing helpers, and other cross-runtime utilities. - Use `@langfuse/shared/src/server` only from server-only web code such as `src/server/**`, `src/pages/api/**`, and server tests. - Use `@langfuse/shared/src/db` only in backend or test code that needs direct Prisma access; never route it into client bundles. - Use narrower subpaths such as `@langfuse/shared/src/env` or `@langfuse/shared/encryption` only when that focused surface is the clearest dependency. - See `../packages/shared/AGENTS.md` for the full shared export map and what each entrypoint contains. - For the higher-level platform topology across web, worker, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis, and S3, also read the architecture handbook: [langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture](https://langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture) with source markdown in `../langfuse-docs/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx` (GitHub mirror: [architecture.mdx](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/4188c1ba453240c90a763a8067ef442d68839323/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx#L4)). ## Package-Local Skills - Shared browser-review workflow for user-visible frontend changes: [`../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md) - Large frontend feature, virtualized-list, local state, and React effect-free data-flow architecture: [`../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md) - Avoidable React effect audits, refactors, and module migrations: [`../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md) - React composition and component API design: [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md) - React/Next.js performance and rendering best practices: [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md) - PostHog product analytics — when and how to instrument user actions: [`../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md) - Sentry error capture — whether and how an error path should report: [`../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md) Read these package-local skills before substantial frontend refactors when the task involves component composition, reusable component APIs, rendering performance, virtualized lists, local feature stores, bundle size, React/Next.js performance patterns, or browser-based signoff of user-visible changes. If you are about to write a `useEffect` or wire form initial values from loaded data, read the frontend-large-feature-architecture skill first — most effects that derive or sync state should not exist. When adding a meaningful user action (button, handler, form, mutation, feature surface), read the PostHog instrumentation skill and decide explicitly whether the action should emit an analytics event. When adding or touching an error path — a `captureException` or `console.error` call, an error boundary, a `catch` block, a Worker `onerror`, or a Sentry `beforeSend`/denylist filter — read the Sentry instrumentation skill first and decide whether it should capture at all (and, for any suppression change, answer "does this rule hide a real error?"). ## Web Conventions - **Before adding or modifying a chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first** — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions (formatting, colors, axis scale, overload) live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Put net-new feature code under `src/features//*`; put broadly reusable components under `src/components/*`. - We use tRPC for full-stack web features; register routers in `src/server/api/root.ts`. - Authentication and RBAC guidance lives in `src/features/rbac/README.md`. - Entitlements guidance lives in `src/features/entitlements/README.md`. - Prefer Shadcn/ui primitives from `src/components/ui`; if a missing component must be installed, ask the user before doing so. - When you surface a score in the UI, always show its level (trace/observation/session/experiment) with the `` component (`src/components/score-tag.tsx`) and its global color coding (see the ScoreTag Storybook story). - Tailwind is the default styling layer; use the shared palette and globals in `src/styles/globals.css`. - Do not add `useEffect` by default. Use it only when a component must synchronize with a concrete system outside React, such as a subscription, browser event listener, observer, timer, or imperative third-party API. Before writing an effect, name that external system and its setup/cleanup lifecycle. If there is no external system, do not use an effect. In particular, do not use effects to derive render state, mirror props or query data into local state, react to user actions, or reset state when an ID changes. Derive during render, run work in the initiating event handler, use query APIs for server state, or mount a keyed child once required data is available. Do not evade this rule with `useLayoutEffect`, a custom wrapper hook, an ESLint suppression, or disabled dependency checks. Use `../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md` for effect work. - In flex layouts, prefer `gap-*` over margin-based `space-x-*`/`space-y-*`. - Treat `!` Tailwind classes as a smell. Step back and fix the owning layout, variant, or primitive before overriding with higher specificity. - When changing shared UI/table patterns, update sibling variants consistently, including default-visible and hidden columns or states. - For component style variants, prefer `cva` with `VariantProps` and merge caller classes through `cn`, following existing `src/components/ui/*` components: ```tsx const cardVariants = cva("rounded-md border", { variants: { intent: { default: "bg-background", error: "border-destructive" }, }, defaultVariants: { intent: "default" }, }); type CardProps = React.HTMLAttributes & VariantProps; const className = cn(cardVariants({ intent }), props.className); ``` - When anchoring sticky, fixed, or absolute elements to the viewport, use `top-banner-offset`, `pt-banner-offset`, `h-screen-with-banner`, or `min-h-screen-with-banner` instead of raw `top-0` so banners do not overlap the UI. - **Z-index / layers — key idea: we are migrating from z-indexes to a layer system** (start of a developing design system; extend it, don't work around it). **To put something on top of something else, use a layer, not a z-index.** The app renders inside `#__next`, isolated into one stacking context (`globals.css`), so its z-indexes can't escape; overlays go in layers that sit outside it and always win. `LAYER_ORDER` is `["panel", "agent", "modal", "popover", "tooltip", "toast"]` — containers declared in `_document.tsx`, ordered by that array (later = on top), carrying NO z-index. `panel` is for docked side surfaces like Sheet, Drawer, and the table peek; `modal` is for true blocking Dialog and AlertDialog surfaces. **THE RULE (see `src/components/ui/layer.tsx` JSDoc — source of truth): every overlay portals through a layer container; never let a Radix/Vaul `*.Portal` fall back to ``.** Radix/Vaul primitives route via their `*.Portal`'s `container` (the `ui/*` wrappers do this with `useLayerContainer`); bespoke imperatively-positioned content renders via ``. z-index stays local to a layer or component (1–2 max), never to escape the app — the `@repo/no-overlay-zindex` lint rule enforces it. - **Overlay lifecycle — a dropdown that opens a modal should close first**, not linger under it (a lifecycle bug, not z-order — don't fix it by re-ranking layers). Radix unmounts a Select/DropdownMenu's content on close, so render the Dialog as a SIBLING (trigger inside, dialog outside), as `useAddLlmConnectionSelect` in `src/components/ModelParameters/index.tsx` does (LFE-10615). - Never import `prettier/plugins/typescript` in client code — it embeds the TypeScript compiler, which the SWC minifier miscompiles (dropped bindings → production-only `ReferenceError`; caught by the CI client-bundle scan, LFE-10645). Format TypeScript with `parser: "babel-ts"` + `prettier/plugins/babel` instead, as the eval-template editor does (`src/features/evals/components/code-eval-template-form-body.tsx`). - Public API routes should use `src/features/public-api/server/withMiddlewares.ts`, define strict request and response types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`, add server tests, and update Fern sources when the contract changes. - Public eval endpoints should keep the split between reusable `evaluators` and ingestion-scoped `evaluation-rules`; do not leak `EvalTemplate` or `JobConfiguration` naming into the public contract. - Keep tests independent; in `src/__tests__/server/**`, prefer scoped cleanup or unique test data over global reset helpers. - Put pure server unit tests that do not need Postgres bootstrap under `src/__tests__/server/unit/**` so they skip the shared DB setup hook. - For small utility functions, prefer Vitest in-source tests when colocated coverage is the simplest option, especially when the test needs access to private implementation details without widening the module API. - Do not extract private utility functions into separate files only to make them testable. Keep them local unless the user explicitly asks for extraction or the utility is meaningfully reused. ## Quick Commands - Dev: `pnpm --filter web run dev` - Lint: `pnpm --filter web run lint` - Lint fix: `pnpm --filter web run lint:fix` - Typecheck: `pnpm --filter web run typecheck` - Server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` - In-source tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:in-source ` - Client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client ` - E2E tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:e2e` - Agent browser install to the default user-level Playwright cache: `pnpm run playwright:install` - Build: `pnpm --filter web run build` ## Playbooks ### Add/Change tRPC endpoint 1. Implement router/procedure in `src/server/api/routers/*` or `src/features//server/*`. 2. Register in `src/server/api/root.ts`. 3. Reuse auth/error patterns from `src/server/api/trpc.ts`. 4. Add/adjust server tests under `src/__tests__/server/*`. ### Add/Change public API endpoint 1. Add route in `src/pages/api/public/*`. 2. Define/update contract types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`. 3. Add/adjust server tests in `src/__tests__/server/*`. 4. If API contract changed, update Fern source (`../fern/apis/**`) and regenerate outputs (do not hand-edit `../generated/**`). ### Error handling (tRPC + REST) 1. Throw `BaseError` subclasses (eg `LangfuseNotFoundError`) from handlers and services. 2. Let `BaseError`s bubble up to the tRPC and REST middlewares (eg. don't `try/catch` and rethrow in to `TRPCError` the handler) 3. Extend the `BaseError` or its subclasses in [`packages/shared/src/errors/`](../packages/shared/src/errors/) as needed. ### Add frontend feature 1. Prefer `src/features//*` for feature-local code. 2. Put broadly reusable components in `src/components/*`. 3. Keep server logic near feature server folders when possible. 4. For meaningful user actions (buttons, form submits, mode switches), decide explicitly whether to instrument them with PostHog. Use `../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`. 5. Review the affected user flow in a real browser with the Playwright MCP server before signoff. Use `../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`. ### Agent browser loop 1. Start the app with `pnpm run dev:web` unless an existing local server is already running. 2. Install Chromium with `pnpm run playwright:install` if Playwright has not been set up on this machine yet. 3. Use the workspace `playwright` MCP server from `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, or `.vscode/mcp.json` for browser-driven review of user-visible frontend changes, not just debugging. 4. {

    "title": "Quality Metrics Observability Standard (Shadow Traffic + Rollouts)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Quality Metrics Observability Standard (Shadow Traffic + Rollouts)\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Allison Grant\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Selene Huang\",\n    \"Sana Farid\",\n    \"Nadia Rahman\",\n    \"Jonas Weber\",\n    \"Logan Wright\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"observability\",\n    \"quality-metrics\",\n    \"shadow-traffic\",\n    \"dashboards\",\n    \"sampling\",\n    \"confidence-intervals\",\n    \"cardinality\",\n    \"rollouts\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-shadow-metrics-data-model-and-cardinality.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/shadow-traffic-slos-and-guardrails.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-scoring-templates-and-rubrics.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/shadow-traffic-data-retention-and-redaction.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-shadow-traffic-routing-architecture.json\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis standard defines how Redwood emits, aggregates, and presents *quality* metrics produced by shadow traffic and rollout experiments. It is intended to make metrics comparable across:\\n- Hosted API\\n- Dedicated\\n- Private (VPC / on-prem)\\n\\nThis document covers:\\n- Metric naming and tagging (dimension) conventions\\n- Sampling math and how to compute unbiased aggregates\\n- Aggregation windows and minimum sample requirements\\n- Confidence interval (CI) and delta reporting requirements\\n- Dashboard conventions and recommended views\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n- The scoring rubric definitions themselves (see rubrics doc)\\n- Data retention/redaction policy details (see security doc)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Control**: The production response returned to the end-user.\\n- **Shadow target / Candidate**: The mirrored variant that does *not* affect the user response (e.g., new model version, quant profile, prompt template).\\n- **Shadow pair**: (control request, control output) + (shadow output) for the same request fingerprint.\\n- **Experiment**: A named configuration that defines sampling, bucketing, and one or more shadow targets.\\n- **Scoring job**: Asynchronous evaluation run over a shadow pair producing metric values.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Guiding principles\\n1. **Comparability > expressiveness**: A small, consistent set of dimensions is preferred over a large set of slice-and-dice tags.\\n2. **Cardinality is a hard constraint**: Any metric that can explode by customer/route/prompt must be bucketed, sampled, or moved to logs/traces.\\n3. **Unbiased aggregates**: Reported rates and means must correctly account for sampling and missingness.\\n4. **CIs are mandatory for quality deltas**: Show uncertainty; do not imply regressions from noisy small samples.\\n5. **Fail-open and isolation**: Observability must never impact the user path; shadow scoring can degrade independently.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Metric naming standard\\nAll emitted metrics for shadow quality must follow:\\n\\n**Prefix**\\n- `ri.shadow.` for shadow-traffic-derived metrics (RI = Redwood Inference)\\n\\n**Namespace**\\n- `quality` (scored rubric metrics)\\n- `pipeline` (ingestion/scoring health)\\n- `sampling` (effective sample sizes, drop reasons)\\n\\n**Metric name format**\\n- `ri.shadow.<namespace>.<metric>`\\n\\nExamples:\\n- `ri.shadow.quality.format_adherence_rate`\\n- `ri.shadow.quality.refusal_rate`\\n- `ri.shadow.quality.instruction_following_score_mean`\\n- `ri.shadow.quality.delta.refusal_rate_pp` (pp = percentage points)\\n- `ri.shadow.pipeline.scoring_lag_seconds_p95`\\n- `ri.shadow.sampling.effective_n`\\n\\n### Suffix conventions\\nUse suffixes consistently:\\n- `_rate` for proportions in [0, 1]\\n- `_pp` for percentage-point deltas (shadow - control) in [-1, 1]\\n- `_mean` for means of bounded continuous scores (typically [0, 1] or [1, 5])\\n- `_p50/_p95/_p99` for quantiles\\n- `_count` for counts\\n- `_seconds` for durations (SI units)\\n\\n### Units and scaling\\n- Rates are stored as decimals (0.02 = 2%). Dashboards may display as percent.\\n- Deltas are expressed as:\\n  - `delta.<metric>_pp` for rate deltas (percentage points)\\n  - `delta.<metric>_mean` for mean deltas\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Dimension (tag/label) conventions\\nDimensions must be limited and consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.\\n\\n### Required dimensions (MUST)\\n| Dimension | Type | Notes |\\n|---|---:|---|\\n| `deployment_mode` | enum | `hosted`, `dedicated`, `private` |\\n| `region` | enum | Redwood region identifier (bucketed set; no arbitrary strings) |\\n| `route_id` | string | Stable opaque ID (NOT the full route path); see cardinality guidance |\\n| `experiment_id` | string | Stable ID for shadow experiment |\\n| `variant_role` | enum | `control`, `shadow` |\\n| `variant_id` | string | Stable ID of model/version/config variant |\\n| `request_type` | enum | `chat`, `generate`, `embeddings` (if applicable), `rerank` (if applicable) |\\n| `rubric_version` | string | E.g., `v1.0.3`; MUST be pinned per experiment run |\\n\\n### Allowed optional dimensions (SHOULD)\\nOnly use when needed for product decisions and already cardinality-reviewed:\\n- `customer_tier`: `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`\\n- `capacity_tier`: `shared`, `reserved` (Dedicated)\\n- `hardware_class`: `h100`, `a100`, `l40s`, etc. (bucketed)\\n- `streaming`: `true`/`false`\\n- `prompt_template_id`: stable small-set ID (MUST be capped; no raw prompt IDs)\\n\\n### Forbidden dimensions (MUST NOT)\\nThese are too high-cardinality or sensitive for metrics:\\n- Raw `customer_id` (use tier, or dedicated tenant ID only if pre-approved)\\n- `user_id`, `session_id`, `conversation_id`\\n- `prompt_id` if derived per-request\\n- Any free-form `error_message` or `model_output` substrings\\n- Full URL paths, unbounded headers, or arbitrary JSON blobs\\n\\n### Cardinality guardrail\\nAll new dimensions MUST be approved in the observability cardinality review and conform to:\\n- `route_id` cardinality per region: target < 5k active IDs\\n- `variant_id` cardinality: target < 500 active IDs\\n- Any optional dimension must have an explicit max set size and documented fallback bucket (`other`)\\n\\nReference: ADR \\u201cshadow metrics data model and cardinality\\u201d.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Sampling standard and math\\nShadow traffic is typically sampled (e.g., 1% of production requests). Aggregations MUST correctly account for sampling and deterministic bucketing.\\n\\n### Sampling mechanism\\nSupported mechanisms:\\n1. **Deterministic bucketing (preferred)**\\n   - Compute a stable fingerprint per request\\n   - Assign to a bucket via consistent hashing\\n   - Shadow if bucket < `sampling_rate`\\n\\n2. **Bernoulli sampling (acceptable for ad-hoc / short runs)**\\n   - Shadow with probability `p` per request\\n   - Higher variance; not stable across time windows\\n\\nStandard requirement:\\n- Experiments intended for time-series comparisons (day-over-day, canary timeline) SHOULD use deterministic bucketing.\\n\\n### Effective sample size (`effective_n`)\\nDefine:\\n- `n_total`: number of eligible production requests\\n- `n_shadowed`: number of requests mirrored to at least one shadow target\\n- `n_scored`: number of shadow pairs successfully scored for a rubric\\n\\nWe emit:\\n- `ri.shadow.sampling.eligible_count`\\n- `ri.shadow.sampling.shadowed_count`\\n- `ri.shadow.sampling.scored_count`\\n- `ri.shadow.sampling.effective_n` (equal to `n_scored` for a given metric/rubric)\\n\\n### Missingness and drop reasons\\nTo avoid biased results, dashboards MUST show drop rates:\\n- `drop_reason=ingestion_lag`\\n- `drop_reason=scoring_timeout`\\n- `drop_reason=redaction_blocked`\\n- `drop_reason=shadow_target_error`\\n- `drop_reason=unsupported_request_type`\\n\\nA quality metric should not be used for go/no-go decisions if:\\n- `scored_count / shadowed_count < 0.90` for the selected window (default threshold)\\n\\n### Unbiased rate estimation under sampling\\nIf sampling rate `p` is constant and applied before scoring, then the *sample mean* over scored items is an unbiased estimate of the population mean **only if** missingness is independent of the outcome. Because scoring failures can correlate with content/length, we require:\\n- Always emit and monitor drop reasons\\n- Prefer deterministic bucketing and stable timeouts\\n- For key metrics used in guardrails, add a \\u201cmissingness sensitivity\\u201d panel (see dashboard section)\\n\\nWhen sampling rates vary across time/regions (e.g., dynamic backpressure), metric computation MUST use per-event weights:\\n- Weight each scored event by `w_i = 1 / p_i` where `p_i` is the effective sampling probability at event time.\\n- Weighted proportion: `p\\u0302 = (\\u03a3 w_i * y_i) / (\\u03a3 w_i)`\\n\\nNote: In v1, sampling is expected to be constant within an experiment run; weighted computation is still required in the analytics layer to be safe under backpressure adjustments.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Aggregation windows and minimum sample sizes\\n### Standard windows\\nDashboards and API aggregates MUST support these rollups:\\n- `1m` (operational/pipeline health only)\\n- `5m` (operational)\\n- `1h` (rollout monitoring)\\n- `24h` (decision-making / stable quality deltas)\\n\\n### Minimum sample requirements for reporting\\nFor quality deltas:\\n- Do not display a delta CI band unless `effective_n >= 200` (per variant per metric per window).\\n- Do not raise regression alerts unless `effective_n >= 500` AND the regression persists for >= 2 consecutive `1h` windows (or one `24h` window).\\n\\nFor rare-event rates (e.g., severe safety violations):\\n- Require `effective_n >= 2000` before concluding \\u201cno regression\\u201d from non-events.\\n- Prefer longer windows and/or higher sampling.\\n\\nThese thresholds are defaults; they may be tightened for enterprise rollouts.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Confidence intervals (CI) and delta reporting\\n### Required outputs for each quality metric\\nFor each (experiment_id, variant_id, metric, window):\\n- Point estimate for control\\n- Point estimate for shadow\\n- Delta = shadow - control\\n- 95% CI for each estimate OR at minimum the 95% CI for the delta\\n- `effective_n` for control and shadow (where applicable)\\n- `rubric_version`\\n\\n### CI methods (standardized)\\n1. **Rates (binary outcomes)**\\n   - Use **Wilson score interval** for each rate.\\n   - For deltas, use either:\\n     - Newcombe method (difference of two Wilson intervals), or\\n     - Bootstrap over paired samples (preferred when pairing is available).\\n\\n2. **Means of bounded scores**\\n   - Use non-parametric bootstrap (default) with 1,000 resamples.\\n   - Report CI for mean and delta.\\n\\n3. **Paired evaluation (recommended)**\\nWhen a shadow pair is scored on the same request fingerprint for both control and shadow outputs, treat deltas as paired:\\n- Compute per-request metric difference `d_i`\\n- Report mean(delta) with bootstrap CI over `d_i`\\n\\nPaired deltas reduce variance and are strongly preferred for rollout decisions.\\n\\n### Display conventions\\n- Always show CI as a shaded band around the delta line (time series) or as whiskers on a point (summary view).\\n- If `effective_n` is below threshold, show the point estimate but gray out the delta and mark as \\u201cinsufficient data\\u201d.\\n\\n### Statistical significance language\\nUI text MUST avoid definitive claims solely based on p-values. Approved terms:\\n- \\u201cLikely regression\\u201d when CI excludes 0 and sample size thresholds met\\n- \\u201cInconclusive\\u201d when CI overlaps 0 or sample size insufficient\\n- \\u201cLikely improvement\\u201d when CI excludes 0 in the positive direction\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Delta metric definitions\\nDelta metrics are always defined as:\\n- `delta = shadow - control`\\n\\nRate deltas:\\n- Store as decimal in [-1, 1]. Display as percentage points.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- Control refusal_rate = 0.020\\n- Shadow refusal_rate = 0.035\\n- Delta refusal_rate_pp = +0.015 (+1.5pp)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Dashboard conventions (Console + internal)\\n### Mandatory dashboard sections for Shadow Experiments\\n1. **Overview**\\n   - Experiment metadata: route, variants, sampling rate, start time, rubric version\\n   - Top-line delta cards: key v1 metrics with status (improve / regress / inconclusive)\\n\\n2. **Quality deltas over time (time series)**\\n   - Delta line + 95% CI band\\n   - Toggle for window (1h / 24h)\\n   - Annotation markers for config changes (sampling, rubric version change, target model update)\\n\\n3. **Quality level comparison (absolute)**\\n   - Control and shadow rates/means side-by-side with CIs\\n   - Helps avoid misinterpretation when control is changing due to traffic shift\\n\\n4. **Data completeness and bias checks**\\n   - scored_count, scoring lag p95, drop_reason breakdown\\n   - \\u201cshadow target error rate\\u201d and \\u201cscoring timeout rate\\u201d panels\\n\\n5. **Segments (cardinality-safe)**\\n   Only include segments from the approved dimension list, defaulting to:\\n   - request_type\\n   - streaming true/false\\n   - region\\n   - hardware_class (if available)\\n\\n6. **Examples (audit-friendly)**\\n   - A sampled set of request fingerprints with redacted prompt context\\n   - Control output vs shadow output vs rubric outcomes\\n   - \\u201cExport examples\\u201d action gated by RBAC\\n\\n### Visualization rules\\n- Use red for regressions, green for improvements, gray for inconclusive.\\n- Always include baseline line at 0 for delta charts.\\n- Do not auto-scale y-axis in a way that hides meaningful changes; recommended: fixed symmetric bounds for rates (e.g., \\u00b15pp) with overflow indicators.\\n\\n### Rollout integration\\nWhen attached to a canary/A-B rollout:\\n- Show quality panels in the rollout timeline beside latency/cost/error panels.\\n- Quality should be **advisory** by default; any automatic gating must explicitly state thresholds and minimum sample sizes.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Cross-environment requirements (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)\\n### Hosted\\n- Default retention windows are short; dashboards should emphasize aggregated metrics over raw examples.\\n- Must use standard Redwood regions and route_id mapping.\\n\\n### Dedicated\\n- May allow longer retention and additional approved dimensions (e.g., dedicated tenant identifier) subject to contract and cardinality review.\\n- Ensure dashboards support per-tenant isolation and export controls.\\n\\n### Private (VPC / on-prem)\\n- Must function with customer-controlled storage/metrics backends.\\n- Dimensions must remain bounded; if a customer adds custom dimensions, they are responsible for cardinality impacts.\\n- CI computation must be available in the local analytics layer (no dependency on hosted services).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Required alerting (quality + pipeline health)\\nThis standard defines what must be alertable; exact thresholds are in the SLO/guardrail doc.\\n\\nMinimum alert categories:\\n- **Pipeline lag**: scoring lag p95 exceeds threshold for N minutes\\n- **Drop spikes**: sudden increase in scoring timeouts or ingestion drops\\n- **Shadow target health**: shadow target error rate spikes (fail-open enforced)\\n- **Quality regression candidate**: delta CI excludes 0 beyond threshold AND sample size criteria met\\n\\nAlerts must link to:\\n- The Shadow Experiment dashboard\\n- The runbook for disable/mitigate\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Implementation checklist (for new metrics / dashboards)\\nBefore shipping a new quality metric to customers:\\n1. Name follows `ri.shadow.quality.*` convention\\n2. Dimensions are only from allowed lists; any additions approved via cardinality review\\n3. Effective sample sizes and drop reasons emitted\\n4. CI method implemented and validated for the metric type\\n5. Dashboard includes completeness panels and CI visualization\\n6. Tested across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes\\n7. Reviewed by Observability (Allison Grant / Nadia Rahman) and Evals (Jonas Weber / Sana Farid)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Change log\\n- 2026-02-20: Clarified paired-delta preference and mandatory completeness panels; added minimum sample thresholds for alerts.\\n- 2026-02-03: Added weighted aggregation requirement to handle dynamic sampling under backpressure.\\n- 2026-01-15: Initial publication (naming, dimensions, windows, CI requirements, dashboard conventions).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_84a9dac9a58d4626aaf08ec637efbff7\"\n}",

      "document_id": "dsid_84a9dac9a58d4626aaf08ec637efbff7",
      "ordinal": 3,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Quality Metrics Observability Standard (Shadow Traffic + Rollouts)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/quality-metrics-observability-standard.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\ncontent : # # purpose this standard defines how redwood emits, aggregates, and presents * quality * metrics produced by shadow traffic and rollout experiments. it is intended to make metrics comparable across : - hosted api - dedicated - private ( vpc / on - prem ) this document covers : - metric naming and tagging ( dimension ) conventions - sampling math and how to compute unbiased aggregates - aggregation windows and minimum sample requirements - confidence interval ( ci ) and delta reporting requirements - dashboard conventions and recommended views out of scope : - the scoring rubric definitions themselves ( see rubrics doc ) - data retention / redaction policy details ( see security doc ) - - -",

document.title: Quality Metrics Observability Standard (Shadow Traffic + Rollouts)
document.content:
{
  "title": "Quality Metrics Observability Standard (Shadow Traffic + Rollouts)",
  "space": "architecture-and-standards",
  "author": "Allison Grant",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-20",
  "reviewers": [
    "Selene Huang",
    "Sana Farid",
    "Nadia Rahman",
    "Jonas Weber",
    "Logan Wright"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "observability",
    "quality-metrics",
    "shadow-traffic",
    "dashboards",
    "sampling",
    "confidence-intervals",
    "cardinality",
    "rollouts"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-shadow-metrics-data-model-and-cardinality.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/shadow-traffic-slos-and-guardrails.json",
    "sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-scoring-templates-and-rubrics.json",
    "sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/shadow-traffic-data-retention-and-redaction.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-shadow-traffic-routing-architecture.json"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This standard defines how Redwood emits, aggregates, and presents *quality* metrics produced by shadow traffic and rollout experiments. It is intended to make metrics comparable across:
- Hosted API
- Dedicated
- Private (VPC / on-prem)

This document covers:
- Metric naming and tagging (dimension) conventions
- Sampling math and how to compute unbiased aggregates
- Aggregation windows and minimum sample requirements
- Confidence interval (CI) and delta reporting requirements
- Dashboard conventions and recommended views

Out of scope:
- The scoring rubric definitions themselves (see rubrics doc)
- Data retention/redaction policy details (see security doc)

---

## Definitions
- **Control**: The production response returned to the end-user.
- **Shadow target / Candidate**: The mirrored variant that does *not* affect the user response (e.g., new model version, quant profile, prompt template).
- **Shadow pair**: (control request, control output) + (shadow output) for the same request fingerprint.
- **Experiment**: A named configuration that defines sampling, bucketing, and one or more shadow targets.
- **Scoring job**: Asynchronous evaluation run over a shadow pair producing metric values.

---

## Guiding principles
1. **Comparability > expressiveness**: A small, consistent set of dimensions is preferred over a large set of slice-and-dice tags.
2. **Cardinality is a hard constraint**: Any metric that can explode by customer/route/prompt must be bucketed, sampled, or moved to logs/traces.
3. **Unbiased aggregates**: Reported rates and means must correctly account for sampling and missingness.
4. **CIs are mandatory for quality deltas**: Show uncertainty; do not imply regressions from noisy small samples.
5. **Fail-open and isolation**: Observability must never impact the user path; shadow scoring can degrade independently.

---

## Metric naming standard
All emitted metrics for shadow quality must follow:

**Prefix**
- `ri.shadow.` for shadow-traffic-derived metrics (RI = Redwood Inference)

**Namespace**
- `quality` (scored rubric metrics)
- `pipeline` (ingestion/scoring health)
- `sampling` (effective sample sizes, drop reasons)

**Metric name format**
- `ri.shadow.<namespace>.<metric>`

Examples:
- `ri.shadow.quality.format_adherence_rate`
- `ri.shadow.quality.refusal_rate`
- `ri.shadow.quality.instruction_following_score_mean`
- `ri.shadow.quality.delta.refusal_rate_pp` (pp = percentage points)
- `ri.shadow.pipeline.scoring_lag_seconds_p95`
- `ri.shadow.sampling.effective_n`

### Suffix conventions
Use suffixes consistently:
- `_rate` for proportions in [0, 1]
- `_pp` for percentage-point deltas (shadow - control) in [-1, 1]
- `_mean` for means of bounded continuous scores (typically [0, 1] or [1, 5])
- `_p50/_p95/_p99` for quantiles
- `_count` for counts
- `_seconds` for durations (SI units)

### Units and scaling
- Rates are stored as decimals (0.02 = 2%). Dashboards may display as percent.
- Deltas are expressed as:
  - `delta.<metric>_pp` for rate deltas (percentage points)
  - `delta.<metric>_mean` for mean deltas

---

## Dimension (tag/label) conventions
Dimensions must be limited and consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

### Required dimensions (MUST)
| Dimension | Type | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `deployment_mode` | enum | `hosted`, `dedicated`, `private` |
| `region` | enum | Redwood region identifier (bucketed set; no arbitrary strings) |
| `route_id` | string | Stable opaque ID (NOT the full route path); see cardinality guidance |
| `experiment_id` | string | Stable ID for shadow experiment |
| `variant_role` | enum | `control`, `shadow` |
| `variant_id` | string | Stable ID of model/version/config variant |
| `request_type` | enum | `chat`, `generate`, `embeddings` (if applicable), `rerank` (if applicable) |
| `rubric_version` | string | E.g., `v1.0.3`; MUST be pinned per experiment run |

### Allowed optional dimensions (SHOULD)
Only use when needed for product decisions and already cardinality-reviewed:
- `customer_tier`: `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`
- `capacity_tier`: `shared`, `reserved` (Dedicated)
- `hardware_class`: `h100`, `a100`, `l40s`, etc. (bucketed)
- `streaming`: `true`/`false`
- `prompt_template_id`: stable small-set ID (MUST be capped; no raw prompt IDs)

### Forbidden dimensions (MUST NOT)
These are too high-cardinality or sensitive for metrics:
- Raw `customer_id` (use tier, or dedicated tenant ID only if pre-approved)
- `user_id`, `session_id`, `conversation_id`
- `prompt_id` if derived per-request
- Any free-form `error_message` or `model_output` substrings
- Full URL paths, unbounded headers, or arbitrary JSON blobs

### Cardinality guardrail
All new dimensions MUST be approved in the observability cardinality review and conform to:
- `route_id` cardinality per region: target < 5k active IDs
- `variant_id` cardinality: target < 500 active IDs
- Any optional dimension must have an explicit max set size and documented fallback bucket (`other`)

Reference: ADR “shadow metrics data model and cardinality”.

---

## Sampling standard and math
Shadow traffic is typically sampled (e.g., 1% of production requests). Aggregations MUST correctly account for sampling and deterministic bucketing.

### Sampling mechanism
Supported mechanisms:
1. **Deterministic bucketing (preferred)**
   - Compute a stable fingerprint per request
   - Assign to a bucket via consistent hashing
   - Shadow if bucket < `sampling_rate`

2. **Bernoulli sampling (acceptable for ad-hoc / short runs)**
   - Shadow with probability `p` per request
   - Higher variance; not stable across time windows

Standard requirement:
- Experiments intended for time-series comparisons (day-over-day, canary timeline) SHOULD use deterministic bucketing.

### Effective sample size (`effective_n`)
Define:
- `n_total`: number of eligible production requests
- `n_shadowed`: number of requests mirrored to at least one shadow target
- `n_scored`: number of shadow pairs successfully scored for a rubric

We emit:
- `ri.shadow.sampling.eligible_count`
- `ri.shadow.sampling.shadowed_count`
- `ri.shadow.sampling.scored_count`
- `ri.shadow.sampling.effective_n` (equal to `n_scored` for a given metric/rubric)

### Missingness and drop reasons
To avoid biased results, dashboards MUST show drop rates:
- `drop_reason=ingestion_lag`
- `drop_reason=scoring_timeout`
- `drop_reason=redaction_blocked`
- `drop_reason=shadow_target_error`
- `drop_reason=unsupported_request_type`

A quality metric should not be used for go/no-go decisions if:
- `scored_count / shadowed_count < 0.90` for the selected window (default threshold)

### Unbiased rate estimation under sampling
If sampling rate `p` is constant and applied before scoring, then the *sample mean* over scored items is an unbiased estimate of the population mean **only if** missingness is independent of the outcome. Because scoring failures can correlate with content/length, we require:
- Always emit and monitor drop reasons
- Prefer deterministic bucketing and stable timeouts
- For key metrics used in guardrails, add a “missingness sensitivity” panel (see dashboard section)

When sampling rates vary across time/regions (e.g., dynamic backpressure), metric computation MUST use per-event weights:
- Weight each scored event by `w_i = 1 / p_i` where `p_i` is the effective sampling probability at event time.
- Weighted proportion: `p̂ = (Σ w_i * y_i) / (Σ w_i)`

Note: In v1, sampling is expected to be constant within an experiment run; weighted computation is still required in the analytics layer to be safe under backpressure adjustments.

---

## Aggregation windows and minimum sample sizes
### Standard windows
Dashboards and API aggregates MUST support these rollups:
- `1m` (operational/pipeline health only)
- `5m` (operational)
- `1h` (rollout monitoring)
- `24h` (decision-making / stable quality deltas)

### Minimum sample requirements for reporting
For quality deltas:
- Do not display a delta CI band unless `effective_n >= 200` (per variant per metric per window).
- Do not raise regression alerts unless `effective_n >= 500` AND the regression persists for >= 2 consecutive `1h` windows (or one `24h` window).

For rare-event rates (e.g., severe safety violations):
- Require `effective_n >= 2000` before concluding “no regression” from non-events.
- Prefer longer windows and/or higher sampling.

These thresholds are defaults; they may be tightened for enterprise rollouts.

---

## Confidence intervals (CI) and delta reporting
### Required outputs for each quality metric
For each (experiment_id, variant_id, metric, window):
- Point estimate for control
- Point estimate for shadow
- Delta = shadow - control
- 95% CI for each estimate OR at minimum the 95% CI for the delta
- `effective_n` for control and shadow (where applicable)
- `rubric_version`

### CI methods (standardized)
1. **Rates (binary outcomes)**
   - Use **Wilson score interval** for each rate.
   - For deltas, use either:
     - Newcombe method (difference of two Wilson intervals), or
     - Bootstrap over paired samples (preferred when pairing is available).

2. **Means of bounded scores**
   - Use non-parametric bootstrap (default) with 1,000 resamples.
   - Report CI for mean and delta.

3. **Paired evaluation (recommended)**
When a shadow pair is scored on the same request fingerprint for both control and shadow outputs, treat deltas as paired:
- Compute per-request metric difference `d_i`
- Report mean(delta) with bootstrap CI over `d_i`

Paired deltas reduce variance and are strongly preferred for rollout decisions.

### Display conventions
- Always show CI as a shaded band around the delta line (time series) or as whiskers on a point (summary view).
- If `effective_n` is below threshold, show the point estimate but gray out the delta and mark as “insufficient data”.

### Statistical significance language
UI text MUST avoid definitive claims solely based on p-values. Approved terms:
- “Likely regression” when CI excludes 0 and sample size thresholds met
- “Inconclusive” when CI overlaps 0 or sample size insufficient
- “Likely improvement” when CI excludes 0 in the positive direction

---

## Delta metric definitions
Delta metrics are always defined as:
- `delta = shadow - control`

Rate deltas:
- Store as decimal in [-1, 1]. Display as percentage points.

Examples:
- Control refusal_rate = 0.020
- Shadow refusal_rate = 0.035
- Delta refusal_rate_pp = +0.015 (+1.5pp)

---

## Dashboard conventions (Console + internal)
### Mandatory dashboard sections for Shadow Experiments
1. **Overview**
   - Experiment metadata: route, variants, sampling rate, start time, rubric version
   - Top-line delta cards: key v1 metrics with status (improve / regress / inconclusive)

2. **Quality deltas over time (time series)**
   - Delta line + 95% CI band
   - Toggle for window (1h / 24h)
   - Annotation markers for config changes (sampling, rubric version change, target model update)

3. **Quality level comparison (absolute)**
   - Control and shadow rates/means side-by-side with CIs
   - Helps avoid misinterpretation when control is changing due to traffic shift

4. **Data completeness and bias checks**
   - scored_count, scoring lag p95, drop_reason breakdown
   - “shadow target error rate” and “scoring timeout rate” panels

5. **Segments (cardinality-safe)**
   Only include segments from the approved dimension list, defaulting to:
   - request_type
   - streaming true/false
   - region
   - hardware_class (if available)

6. **Examples (audit-friendly)**
   - A sampled set of request fingerprints with redacted prompt context
   - Control output vs shadow output vs rubric outcomes
   - “Export examples” action gated by RBAC

### Visualization rules
- Use red for regressions, green for improvements, gray for inconclusive.
- Always include baseline line at 0 for delta charts.
- Do not auto-scale y-axis in a way that hides meaningful changes; recommended: fixed symmetric bounds for rates (e.g., ±5pp) with overflow indicators.

### Rollout integration
When attached to a canary/A-B rollout:
- Show quality panels in the rollout timeline beside latency/cost/error panels.
- Quality should be **advisory** by default; any automatic gating must explicitly state thresholds and minimum sample sizes.

---

## Cross-environment requirements (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
### Hosted
- Default retention windows are short; dashboards should emphasize aggregated metrics over raw examples.
- Must use standard Redwood regions and route_id mapping.

### Dedicated
- May allow longer retention and additional approved dimensions (e.g., dedicated tenant identifier) subject to contract and cardinality review.
- Ensure dashboards support per-tenant isolation and export controls.

### Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Must function with customer-controlled storage/metrics backends.
- Dimensions must remain bounded; if a customer adds custom dimensions, they are responsible for cardinality impacts.
- CI computation must be available in the local analytics layer (no dependency on hosted services).

---

## Required alerting (quality + pipeline health)
This standard defines what must be alertable; exact thresholds are in the SLO/guardrail doc.

Minimum alert categories:
- **Pipeline lag**: scoring lag p95 exceeds threshold for N minutes
- **Drop spikes**: sudden increase in scoring timeouts or ingestion drops
- **Shadow target health**: shadow target error rate spikes (fail-open enforced)
- **Quality regression candidate**: delta CI excludes 0 beyond threshold AND sample size criteria met

Alerts must link to:
- The Shadow Experiment dashboard
- The runbook for disable/mitigate

---

## Implementation checklist (for new metrics / dashboards)
Before shipping a new quality metric to customers:
1. Name follows `ri.shadow.quality.*` convention
2. Dimensions are only from allowed lists; any additions approved via cardinality review
3. Effective sample sizes and drop reasons emitted
4. CI method implemented and validated for the metric type
5. Dashboard includes completeness panels and CI visualization
6. Tested across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes
7. Reviewed by Observability (Allison Grant / Nadia Rahman) and Evals (Jonas Weber / Sana Farid)

---

## Change log
- 2026-02-20: Clarified paired-delta preference and mandatory completeness panels; added minimum sample thresholds for alerts.
- 2026-02-03: Added weighted aggregation requirement to handle dynamic sampling under backpressure.
- 2026-01-15: Initial publication (naming, dimensions, windows, CI requirements, dashboard conventions).

# Candidate: raw-value histogram binning

Fixes issue #15208 by computing min, range, and bucket membership from raw scores while retaining two-decimal rounding only for display labels. Adds the seven-bin 0.857 regression and an integer-score preservation case.

# Candidate: count-weighted average rollups

Fixes issue #15208 by recombining grouped averages as sum(avg * count) / sum(count) when a count metric is present. Rows missing either member are excluded; zero total count returns zero. Without a count metric, the documented legacy unweighted mean remains. Count/sum/min/max/percentile behavior is unchanged.

Focused regressions cover unequal groups, fallback without counts, subtotal/grand-total behavior, missing paired values, and empty data.

item.text: Implementation is complete on both isolated candidates. The weighted candidate follows the validation standard’s “unbiased aggregates” principle and pairs each group mean only with its own available count; the histogram candidate keeps the presentation decision (rounded labels) separate from the measurement decision (raw-value bin membership). I’m indexing the source, regressions, and candidate notes now, then I’ll review merge previews before publication.

item.text:
Resolved and published both independent fixes to `person/sana-farid`.

- Histogram fix: bucket membership, minimum, and range now use raw values; only display labels are rounded. Added the seven-bin `0.857` regression plus integer-score preservation coverage.
- Aggregation fix: grouped averages now use `Σ(avg × count) / Σ(count)` when a count metric exists. Missing pairs are excluded, zero total count returns zero, and absence of a count metric retains the documented unweighted fallback. Non-average aggregation logic is unchanged.

Evidence used:

- `/code/upstream-issues/langfuse-15208.md` (`enterprise_452a1a7f3eb80e14cfc4d7a0`)
- `/code/langfuse/web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Quality Metrics Observability Standard (`dsid_84a9dac9a58d4626aaf08ec637efbff7`)

Publication:

- Histogram operation: `langfuse-15208-histogram-reviewed`
- Weighted operation: `langfuse-15208-weighted-reviewed`
- Both merges committed successfully.
- All six changed source, test, and candidate-note files were re-indexed.
- Candidate notes published under `/artifacts/`.
- Temporary candidate branches deleted.

Memory saved as `langfuse-15208-corrected-analytics-contracts`, recording both corrected analytics contracts and their evidence.

Remaining validation: the narrow Vitest commands and lint could not run because the mounted snapshot contains no Node or `pnpm` executable (`pnpm: command not found`). Once a toolchain is available, run:

```bash
pnpm --filter web run test src/__tests__/server/unit/score-analytics-utils.servertest.ts
pnpm --filter web run test src/__tests__/server/pivot-table-utils.servertest.ts
pnpm --filter web run lint
```
